fields.rationale: States cluster by their definitional approach: some define surgery broadly by what happens to tissue (cut/altered/infiltrated), some anchor it to invasiveness plus named lasers, some use the anesthetic required as the threshold, some define it primarily by listing excluded procedures, some use instrument-and-closure language, and a few offer only minimal or vague text.

assignments.raw_value: an invasive procedure in which human tissue is cut, ablated, or otherwise penetrated by incision, laser, or other means to treat diseases of the human eye, alter or correct refractive error, or alter or enhance cosmetic appearance; does not include removal of superficial foreign bodies
Invasive surgery including injections into the eyeball, cataract surgery, muscle surgery, retinal surgery, radial keratotomy, laser surgery, and cryosurgery.
Surgery of the lid, adnexa, or visual system which requires anything other than a topical anesthetic is excluded from optometric practice.

An invasive procedure in which in vivo human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, removed, coagulated or photodisrupted by use of an electrical cautery, a scalpel, a cryoprobe, a laser or ionizing radiation; does not include nonsurgical procedures including removal of superficial foreign bodies or eyelashes or use of lasers for diagnostic purposes.

Surgery means any act in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by any means. It does not mean an act that solely involves the administration or prescribing of a topical or oral therapeutic pharmaceutical.
any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical or laser means

The practice of advanced optometric care does not include surgical treatment of glaucoma, treatment of ocular cancer, treatment of infectious diseases of the retina, use of therapeutic lasers, surgical procedures other than noninvasive procedures, use of general anesthesia, use of intravenous injections, procedures that require the cutting or opening of the globe, enucleation of the eye, extraocular muscle surgery or any invasive procedure performed on the human body other than noninvasive procedures performed on the eye or ocular adnexae.

A procedure using an instrument, including a laser, scalpel, or needle, in which human tissue is cut, burned, scraped except as provided in s. 463.014(4), or vaporized, by incision, injection, ultrasound, laser, infusion, cryotherapy, or radiation. The term includes a procedure using an instrument which requires the closure of human tissue by suture, clamp, or other such device.
Any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical or laser means.

Surgical procedures requiring injectable or general anesthesia, moderate sedation, penetration of the globe, or the use of ophthalmic lasers for ophthalmic surgery within or upon the globe; also specifically prohibited: removal of pterygia and Salzmann's nodules, incisional corneal refractive surgery, and strabismus surgery.
therapeutic lasers
Surgery, including the use of lasers for surgical purposes, is excluded from optometric practice, with enumerated exceptions for minor procedures.

Surgical procedures are within scope except specifically excluded nonlaser and laser procedures listed in KRS 320.210(2)(b), including retina laser, LASIK, PRK, enucleation, full-thickness corneal/scleral incision, penetrating keratoplasty, iris/ciliary body incision, vitreous incision, retina incision, crystalline lens extraction, intraocular implants, extraocular muscle surgery, eyelid malignancy/cosmetic/mechanical surgery, bony orbit surgery, lacrimal system surgery (except probing), full-thickness conjunctivoplasty, nonlaser surgery not correcting ocular abnormalities, posterior chamber i

A procedure upon the human eye in which in vivo human tissue is injected, cut, burned, frozen, sutured, vaporized, coagulated, or photodisrupted by the use of surgical instrumentation such as, but not limited to, a scalpel, cryoprobe, laser, electric cautery, or ionizing radiation.
invasive surgical procedures

a procedure using any instruments, including lasers, scalpels, needles, cautery, a cryoprobe, or sutures in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, removed, or otherwise permanently altered by any mechanical means, laser, ionizing radiation, ultrasound, or other means
invasive surgery

Invasive procedures means: use of lasers other than for observation; use of ionizing radiation; use of therapeutic ultrasound; administration of medication by injection; procedures that include an incision.
invasive surgery including, but not limited to, surgery using lasers
Surgery includes the use of lasers for treatment of any disease or condition or for the correction of refractive error.
invasive surgery including laser surgery
invasive surgery
Surgery and laser surgery are excluded from the practice of optometry; infantile/congenital glaucoma treatment is also excluded.

Any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical means, including use of lasers for therapeutic and photorefractive purposes, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, or medication administered by injection

Surgery generally prohibited except for enumerated in-office minor surgical procedures: non-laser removal/destruction/drainage of superficial eyelid lesions and conjunctival cysts; removal of nonperforating foreign bodies; non-laser corneal debridement, culture, scrape or anterior puncture (excluding pterygium, corneal biopsy, or corneal neoplasia removal); removal of eyelashes; probing, dilation, irrigation or closure of tear drainage structures; scalpel use limited to skin surrounding the eye.

Any procedure using a laser, scalpel, needle or other instrument in which any human tissue is cut, burned or vaporized by incision, injection, ultrasound, laser, infusion, cryotherapy, radiation or other means; or any procedure using an instrument which requires the closure of human tissue by suture, clamp or similar device

Invasive modality means any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical or other means; includes surgery, lasers, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound and the removal of foreign bodies from within the tissue of the eye.

Any procedure that involves cutting or otherwise infiltrating human tissue by mechanical means including surgery, laser surgery, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, administering medication by injection, or the removal of intraocular foreign bodies.

Laser surgery procedures are authorized except those involving the retina, LASIK, and cosmetic lid surgery; nonlaser surgery procedures are those authorized by the Oklahoma Board of Examiners in Optometry pursuant to rules under the Administrative Procedures Act.
invasive or laser surgery

Surgery including, but not limited to, diagnostic, exploratory, palliative, therapeutic, rehabilitative, cosmetic, reconstructive, refractive, light-based or laser surgery; or the use of lasers for therapeutic purposes.

Surgery is not explicitly defined in the statute; the prohibition references 'surgery or other invasive techniques' in the context of pharmaceutical agent use, and separately prohibits surgery for detecting diseased or pathological conditions of the eye.

An invasive procedure using instruments that require closure by suturing, clamping, or other similar devices, or a procedure in which the presence or assistance of a nurse anesthetist or an anesthesiologist is required.

Surgery excludes optometric practice scope; the term 'any means or method' does not include surgeries unless otherwise permitted by this chapter; intraocular surgery and refractive surgery are explicitly prohibited
any surgical procedure requiring other than a topical anesthetic; cataract surgery and radial keratotomy are specifically named prohibitions

A procedure using instruments, including lasers, scalpels, or needles, in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, or otherwise altered by any mechanical means, laser, or ionizing radiation. Includes procedures using instruments that require closing by suturing, clamping, or another device. Does not include a noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in the conjunctiva, eyelid, or corneal epithelium that has not perforated the Bowman's membrane.
Surgery in which human tissue is cut, burned, or vaporized by means of laser or ionizing radiation (for laser surgery)
Treatment through revision, destruction, incision or other structural alteration of human tissue using laser technology, or incision/excision of ocular structures as enumerated in § 54.1-3201(B)(1).

Any invasive procedure in which human tissue is cut, ablated, or otherwise penetrated by incision, injection, laser, ultrasound, or other means, in order to treat human eye diseases, alter or correct refractive error, or alter or enhance cosmetic appearance.

Excluded surgical procedures include surgery with general anesthesia, removal of an eye, surgery of the bony orbit, incisional/excisional surgery of extraocular muscles, eyelid surgery for malignancies or cosmetic/mechanical repair, incisional surgery of lacrimal system (other than probing), full thickness conjunctivoplasty with graft/flap, pterygium surgery, full thickness incision/excision of cornea/sclera (other than emergency paracentesis), corneal transplants, incision of iris or ciliary body, surgical extraction of crystalline lens, intraocular implants, vitreous removal, vitreous chambe
